transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you to the clinic today?

I've come in because I've been losing a lot of weight lately. Honestly, I'm barely eating anything these days, sometimes just a bite or two of food a day. My family insisted I get checked out because of it.
Do you feel very afraid of gaining weight, or do you think you are overweight even when others say you are too thin?

Yes, I am absolutely terrified of gaining any weight, and even the thought of it makes me incredibly anxious. When I look in the mirror, I still see myself as fat and feel like I need to lose more, even though everyone else tells me I'm already too thin.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Anorexia Nervosa, Major Depressive Disorder, Persistent Depressive Disorder], but the patient now clearly endorses intense fear of gaining weight, persistent restriction of intake, and distorted body image despite being underweight. These findings strongly support Anorexia Nervosa, while Major Depressive Disorder and Persistent Depressive Disorder are no longer the best explanations for the core presentation.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports marked restriction of food intake with significant weight loss, intense fear of gaining weight, and distorted body image with perceiving herself as fat despite being visibly underweight. These core features are most consistent with anorexia nervosa.
